subject: strategy
text:
| Signal | Coverage focus | Tier-specific depth (viola v1) |
|--------|---------------|---------------------|
| Spans / Traces | The 6 must-trace paths (Section 4) and every crate seam: `viola-pty` spawn/write/wait/kill, `viola-channel` client call and server dispatch, `viola-state` snapshot/heartbeat/tail, `viola-agent-claude` hook parse, `viola-mcp` tool calls | Declared in code with tracing 0.1.44 `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "<area>.<operation>", fields(...))]`. They are **not serialized** in v1, because the output sets `with_current_span(false)` + `with_span_list(false)`. They give the code its structure and are ready for the deferred tracing-opentelemetry 0.34.0 bridge. Cross-process joins use `corr` + `conn`, not W3C trace IDs |

subject: strategy
text: | Structured Logs | Every boundary call, state transition, refusal, fault/heal and process lifecycle, as the closed `event` enum (Section 3) | **The primary signal.** tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 JSON-per-line, one file per process role under `<home>/diagnostics/`, merged with `events.ndjson` by `agent-run logs` |

subject: strategy
text: | Errors | Panics (a one-line `event:"panic"` record), typed thiserror 2.0.20 errors with fixed `Display`, exit codes plus distinct `detail` codes on `process-exit` | No external reporter: security says "no outbound network calls". A hand-written `std::panic::set_hook`, plus `std::panic::catch_unwind` at the main-thread catch site of every role, around `hook` dispatch, in the `run` PTY pump and handle-wait threads, and around the vt100 feed (Section 7) |

subject: strategy
text: | Metrics | `duration_ms` samples, counts of `event`/`detail` values, `skipped` counts | No in-process instruments and no exporter. Metrics are derived by `jq` over the ndjson; the perf gates run on hyperfine 1.20.0 `--export-json` (Section 5) |

subject: strategy
text: | Audit Logs | `instances/<name>/events.ndjson` is the product audit stream (arch-owned, never rotated) | Not a compliance trail (security Minimal, no compliance triggers). Obs never copies event payloads into process logs |

subject: strategy
text: - Every panic after init step 4 produces exactly one single-line structured record in its home-level role file: location, thread, role and instance. The bounded exemptions (the pre-init window, `cli` without an instance, `hook` without `VIOLA_NAME`, a failed step-4 role-file open, the no-obs-init hidden capture arms (`hook <event> --capture` and `hook statusline --capture`), and a refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`) or on `viola hook statusline`, or a refused `viola list` scan, which opens none either) are listed in Section 10. The payload (one escaped JSON string) and the backtrace (a one-line JSON array of frames) are written only to the instance-scoped detail file (Section 7).
